verdict.rationale: Temporal ships an official CLI for managing, monitoring and debugging applications. It can start an embedded dev service (`temporal server start-dev`), list namespaces and workflows from the command line, and deploy via Docker or Kubernetes, all of which support headless, scriptable operation. No evidence explicitly documents CI usage such as pipeline recipes, non-interactive auth for CI, or test-server patterns. missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline integration docs, non-interactive/headless auth guidance for automation, hands-on corroboration of CI use

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use it to manage, monitor, and debug Temporal applications, plus run an embedded development service when you need fast local feedback.

temporal operator namespace list
temporal workflow list

brew install temporal
temporal server start-dev
Choose a deployment approach (Docker, Kubernetes, or manual) and set up a production-ready Temporal Service.
